subject: Sizing request: Dedicated POC for 64k-context model — memory headroom & quantization
messages:
From: Alex Guerrero <alex.guerrero@novacorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing question for Dedicated POC: 64k context models

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to set up a short Dedicated POC to validate latency and cost for a multi-turn retrieval assistant built on a 70B-class open model with 64k context. A few specifics from our side:
- Expected steady concurrency: ~5 concurrent users (mostly interactive).
- Peak concurrency: up to 20 simultaneous requests during business spikes.
- Typical request: 1k tokens prompt (including retrieved context), ~512 tokens generated.
- We plan to use persistent KV cache per session where possible.

Can you help us understand the GPU headroom we should reserve, especially how the KV cache and different quantization modes (int8 / int4) affect GPU memory and fleet sizing? Also flag anything that would materially change cost/SLA.

We'd like a short runbook and an estimate we can include in our procurement conversation.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Guerrero
Head of Product Engineering, NovaCorp
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Guerrero <alex.guerrero@novacorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question for Dedicated POC: 64k context models

Alex — thanks, this is helpful context. High-level answers up front, detail and numbers below. Happy to schedule an hour with SEs to walk through the numbers.

Short answer: KV cache for 64k context materially increases per-request memory needs; quantization reduces model weights but has diminishing returns on KV cache size. For your profile (steady 5, spikes to 20), we should scope a reserved pool for the steady baseline with autoscale headroom for spikes.

Quick clarifying asks before we finalize estimates:
- Will most sessions reuse KV across multiple requests (persistent session cache) or are you more often starting fresh?
- Are you comfortable with an int8 quantization baseline for pilot (we'll provide quality/regen tests), or do you need to evaluate int4 first?
- Any hard latency SLO (p50/p95 targets) for generation?

I'll pull together a rough GPU count and an internal sketch, and loop in KarThik (SE) and Marissa (solutions) to sign off on the rollout plan.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NovaCorp 64k context sizing sketch (please review)

Hi team,
Looping you in to build a concise capacity recommendation for the customer and procurement. Below are the assumptions Alex gave and my early-ballpark numbers — please adjust:

Assumptions from NovaCorp:
- Model class: 70B-ish open model baseline (we'll confirm exact artifact).
- Context: 64k tokens (retrieval-backed).
- Typical request/response: 1k prompt / 512 gen.
- Concurrency: steady 5, peak 20.

Important notes:
1) Model weights vs KV cache: model weights sit in GPU memory (reduced by quantization). KV cache grows with sequence length independent of weight quantization; with long context KV can quickly dominate per-request memory.
2) Quantization impact (rough guidance):
   - FP16 baseline (no quant): weights ~40–48 GB for 70B;
   - int8 QA (q8/4 variants): weights ~22–28 GB;
   - int4 aggressive: weights ~14–20 GB (more model-dependent and requires eval).
3) KV cache: for 64k context we estimate KV cache contribution in the ballpark of ~30–60 GB of RAM per concurrent request for 70B-class models depending on implementation (packed vs per-layer storing) and whether we use prefix compression / chunked offload. This is the asymmetry — even with int8 weights you still need headroom for KV.

Preliminary sizing thought:
- Baseline reserved pool for steady 5 concurrent sessions: prefer 2 x 80GB-GPU nodes (each node can host 2 steady sessions with reduced-precision weights and some KV sharing), plus autoscale to handle spikes.
- Autoscale headroom: plan for capacity to hit 20 concurrent sessions — roughly 6–8 x 80GB GPUs (estimate depends on how aggressively we quantize and whether we allow KV offload to host memory or NVMe).
- If customer accepts int8 and we enable KV prefix caching + per-session persistence, we can reduce required GPUs by ~25–40% compared to FP16 baseline. Int4 might reduce weight memory further but doesn't proportionally reduce KV cache, and quality needs to be validated.

Operational asks for POC:
- We'll run short microbenchmarks with their exact model artifact and a 64k simulated trace — that will give precise per-token KV numbers and throughput.
- Need sample request traces (token distribution, session lengths) or a synthetic trace if they cannot share production logs.
- We'll provide a small deliverable: 1-page headroom table + expected cost delta vs hosted.

I'll attach a draft estimator and we can refine — KarThik, anything you'd change on headroom math / autoscale assumptions?

— Naomi

From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: NovaCorp 64k context sizing sketch (please review)

Nice summary Naomi — a few concrete adjustments from SE perspective:

- Concrete autoscale proposal: reserve for steady baseline (2x 80GB A100-style GPUs) and allow autoscale up to an 8-node pool for spikes. Empirically, with int8 we see ~2 sessions per 80GB GPU for heavy-KV 64k workloads; with FP16 it's 1 session per GPU.
- KV offload options: if we allow NVMe-backed chunked KV offload we can push per-GPU concurrency up by ~1.5x at the cost of increased p95 latency for tokens that miss in hot cache. Recommend NVMe offload as an option in Dedicated POC so NovaCorp can see tradeoffs.
- Quality vs quantization: plan an A/B eval on a representative prompt set. Recommend starting with int8 for pilot; only move to int4 if the metric delta < 2% on our regressions.
- Safety margin: add ~20% memory headroom for peak transient KV growth and internal tracing hooks.

I'll attach a quick estimator (spreadsheet) with the node counts + cost delta scenarios. Marissa — can you coordinate the MSA language around autoscale and burst capacity (we should call out NVMe offload and quantization support)?

— KarThik
From: Alex Guerrero <alex.guerrero@novacorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question for Dedicated POC: 64k context models

Thanks Naomi, KarThik — this is exactly what we needed to move procurement. We approve a pilot that reserves the steady baseline you recommended (2x 80GB GPUs) and enables autoscale up to 8 nodes. Please include NVMe offload as an option in the POC and run the int8 baseline evaluation.

Next steps:
- Naomi: send the 1-page headroom table and the estimator (spreadsheet) to procurement (copied).
- Marissa: we need a short appendix for the SOW listing burst headroom, quantization caveats, and the evaluation plan.
- Procurement: once we have the cost delta and SOW we can push the PO next week.

Appreciate the quick turn.

— Alex
